chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in combining in the voluntary prayer whatever surahs you wish."

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What surahs can be recited in voluntary prayers?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and transmitted through the chain of Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the juristic flexibility in voluntary (nafl) prayers, distinguishing them from the fixed recitations often preferred in obligatory prayers. It underscores the principle that while specific surahs like Al-Fatiha are essential, the choice of additional chapters is left to the worshipper’s discretion, reflecting the ease (yusr) intended in supererogatory acts of worship.
